bottom_line: May 2026 OFAC Operation Economic Fury sharply raises enforcement-attention risk for EU correspondent banks with UAE/HK-routed flows; tighten EDD on shell-company typology now, ahead of likely follow-on actions.
what_changed: On 2026-05-01 OFAC designated 35 entities and individuals tied to Iran's shadow-banking architecture and explicitly named Hong Kong and the UAE as preferred shell-company jurisdictions for the Zarringhalam network (Treasury press release SB-0477).
why_it_matters: The legal risk surface for non-US correspondent banks did not change materially, but the enforcement-attention surface did. Adjacency risk through cover-company patterns matching the published typology now drives short-horizon EDD posture.
affected_actors: EU correspondent banks with UAE/HK/TR exposure
Iranian rahbar networks and front companies
main_uncertainty: Whether OFAC or aligned EU/UK authorities will name a financial intermediary in a follow-on designation within the 90-day horizon, and how quickly correspondent-bank partners formalize typology-based EDD requests.

scenarios.name: Typology absorption
scenarios.description: OFAC publishes follow-on FAQs; EU/UK regulators issue typology guidance; correspondent partners tighten EDD voluntarily.
indicators: HK SFC or UAE Central Bank circulars

scenarios.name: Intermediary-bank designation
scenarios.description: OFAC names a specific correspondent or payment intermediary tied to the typology.
indicators: Further OFAC press releases under Operation Economic Fury
Secondary reporting of named banks in HK/UAE

scenarios.name: Allied alignment
scenarios.description: EU or UK adds aligned designations or sectoral measures on the same network.

scenarios.name: Quiet status quo
scenarios.description: No follow-on action, no aligned moves over the 90-day horizon.
indicators: Absence of OFAC follow-up within 60 days

watch_next: Further OFAC press releases referencing SB-0477 or Operation Economic Fury
EU consolidated sanctions list updates touching the same network
HK SFC or UAE Central Bank typology bulletins
Correspondent-partner EDD letters citing the Zarringhalam typology
Naming of any financial intermediary in a follow-on action
